page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The platform delivers 192 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock of 2.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes no integrated local storage and operates without discrete GPUs, depending entirely on remote EBS volumes for block storage. Network capabilities are provisioned with a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput. Multi-core compute performance sits in the top tier across stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation metrics, alongside high bzip3 decompression throughput. Memory subsystem testing confirms massive bandwidth, exceeding 890 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 425 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-thread performance metrics, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core results, place in the middle 50% category. In-memory data store operations such as Redis SET commands and static web serving throughput also demonstrate top-tier execution.

The hardware configuration provides high compute density and energy efficiency due to its bare-metal ARM architecture and dedicated physical core structure. Because there is no local NVMe storage and no hardware acceleration for machine learning, tasks relying heavily on local disk I/O or token generation in large language models present clear tradeoffs. Workloads best suited for this instance include large-scale multi-threaded compilation pipelines, distributed databases, large memory caching clusters, container fleet hosts, and high-concurrency web microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.7 GHz, 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect top-tier multi-threaded processing capacity, high memory bandwidth, and rapid data store transactions, balanced by moderate single-threaded execution speeds. Operating without hypervisor overhead, it maximizes physical core utilization and cache coherency. Given its high core density, vast DDR5 memory pool, and baseline network throughput, the m8g.metal-48xl is suitable for high-concurrency web serving, large Redis caching tiers, distributed database engines, software build farms, and dense multi-tenant container orchestration.
